questions.label: (a)
questions.prompt: (a) Describe the chemical test for water using anhydrous copper(II) sulfate. Include the starting colour and the positive result. [2]
questions.answer: Add anhydrous copper(II) sulfate: it turns from white to blue if water is present.

questions.label: (b)
questions.prompt: (b) A liquid boils sharply at 100 °C at standard atmospheric pressure. Explain what ths suggests about the purity of the water. [2]
questions.answer: It is pure water, because a pure substance boils at a fixed temperature.

questions.label: (a)
questions.prompt: (a) Describe a safe method for carrying out a flame test on a solid salt. Your method should include how the wire loop is cleaned. [3]
questions.answer: Clean the loop in concentrated HCl, dip it in the salt and hold it in the hot blue flame; observe the colour.

questions.label: (b)
questions.prompt: (b) Explain why the wire loop must be cleaned before testing a new sample. [1]
questions.answer: To remove traces of the previous sample so its colour does not contaminate the result.

questions.label: (a)
questions.prompt: (a) Describe how to test an aqueous sample for chloride ions. State the reagent(s) and the positive observation. [2]
questions.answer: Add dilute nitric acid then silver nitrate solution; a white precipitate shows chloride.

questions.label: (b)
questions.prompt: (b) Write the ionic equation, including state symbols, for the formation of silver chloride. [2]
